thread.title: The Hot Stove Keeps Burning - The Idea Guide

author: The Idea Guide
title: The Hot Stove Keeps Burning - The Idea Guide
text:
By Daniel Shvartsman
This week's Idea Guide - apologies for missing our midweek publication - has a lot of material to work from. Though you might think this is a dead zone for investors, authors have been keeping us busy with plenty of investing ideas. And though the renewed burst to all-time highs would seem to stretch valuations, it does seem like there are more ideas shaking out that could be of interest to investors of all stripes. I start with short ideas here but find five on each side of the aisle that may be worth your time to review.
Short Ideas We published 23 short ideas from last Friday through Thursday. 7 of them are on Tesla ( TSLA ), a recent high as the SEC, Elon Musk, and various large sources of money have failed to put us out of our misery yet.
We published several interesting short ideas, though, and I wanted to flag a few.
Sunrun: Nothing New Under The Sun by Investor Gator Sunrun ( RUN ) has made a prodigious move this year, up 2.5x so far in 2018. Investor Gator takes a closer look at the company's numbers. While Sunrun talks about cash generation and a meaningful net present value from each new customer acquired, Gator looks at the cash flow statements themselves to call out serious cash burn. There is a tax subsidy issue that supports Sunrun's development despite the cash burn, but Gator argues there won't be much left over for actual shareholders.
Where to go next - I would love to see how a bull looks at these numbers or other numbers to make the case that this will work out for shareholders. There may be a different point of emphasis, but the math in this article is compelling.
Sentiment Check - Recently, we have had more bullish sentiment, with three long ideas this year (and early enough in the year that they were not just chasing price) to one short idea. Sunrun took a lot of heat in 2015-2016 from our authors but has been less in the spotlight since.
Trupanion: A Moonshot Valuation With Lingering Questions by the Capitolist This article follows up the Capitolist's first article on Trupanion ( TRUP ). Trupanion has been a popular target for short-sellers, and one of those stocks that has flown in the face of such targeting. I think what is noteworthy in this case is the author's reporting of the company's negative response to their original article and the tone in the company's emails. Without getting into the specifics of the regulatory thesis - how strong will regulation be in the pet insurance space? - I find that a noteworthy and concerning response as far as the focus of the company.
Where to go next - Trupanion has soared without much peer in their industry. Are there others looking to grow a pet insurance business, and what does the competitive landscape look like?
Sentiment Check - The rare case where we publish more short-leaning or skeptical analysis than bullish ideas on a stock.
Spotify Is A Serf Whose Liberation Will Never Come by EASTERLY I'm a sucker for a drawn out metaphor, which EASTERLY pulls here with the serfdom approach. Spotify ( SPOT ) is in the hock to the music labels, which restricts it from growing its revenue, goes the argument.
I am a little skeptical that the music labels hold the strong hand here - in an industry where most of the artist earnings go to live performances, it's not clear why the record label itself can own distribution over something like Spotify that actually has the listeners. But the competition from YouTube ( GOOG ), Apple ( AAPL ), Amazon ( AMZN ), and others does seem to loom large for Spotify, and so this article adds a useful perspective to that.
Where to go next - As the author points out, the labels used to own stakes in Spotify but have been decreasing those stakes. Thinking through how the negotiating power is shared between these two entities may be the key to understanding SPOT's prospects.
Sentiment Check - We have published seven long ideas on SPOT and this is our first pure short idea on the company. Despite its ubiquity on our phones, Spotify hasn't yet attracted the conversation of a company like Netflix ( NFLX ), its commonly cited video analogue.
Red Robin: Significantly Overvalued Even After The Fall by Detroit Bear Restaurants can be dangerous because they seem so understandable and sometimes offer real value but are often flash in the pan. Also, scuttlebutt research can be hard on the body. Red Robin ( RRGB ) comes into Detroit Bear's sights and comes out with 25% downside in the author's view. The basic issue is that comps are getting worse, and the cost climate is as well. Declining sales and increasing costs is not a good situation even at 5-6x EV/EBITDA, and for a regional chain, the direction is especially worrying because it's not clear that there is a bottom. Especially when the industry itself has seemed to stabilize, as Bear points out.
Where to go next - This should be an industry where it's easy to stack rank peers against each other, so I would consider looking at other burger chains. Since I'm in Michigan for the week, I'm obligated to point out that Culver's would be a good place to go next as well.
Sentiment Check - It looks like we have two other short or bearish authors on RRGB, vs. two bullish authors. Given RRGB's chart looks like it has taken three meaningful hits in the past 12 months, that's not surprising.
And briefly, I want to share Indo Count - Uncomfortable Times by KR Capital. It's not really a short idea - the author tabs the company as a sell. But it is a nice basic report on an India based company, so for anyone looking to orient themselves, this may be an interesting off the beaten path read.
Long Ideas We published 283 long ideas over the Friday-Thursday period, as nobody is taking a summer vacation. I'm going to go high low here, looking at two popular names and then three more under the radar names.
Tencent: Get Ready To Party Like It's 2009 by JP Research I'm using this article as the stand-in for Tencent ( OTCPK:TCEHY ) coverage because it was easily our most read long idea of the week, but we published several articles on the stock. To wit:
3 Reasons To Buy Tencent Stock Now Tencent: Growth Is Still Strong, But Not Cheap Tencent - A Strong Buy After Disappointing Earnings Rare Entry Into One Of China's Largest Tech Giants Fortnite Is Tencent's Value Creation At Work Tencent has become the slightly 'cooler' way to get China exposure, as investors raise question about Alibaba's ( BABA ) business model and exposure, and stocks like JD.Com ( JD ) fail to reward value investor hopes. And of course, Naspers ( OTCPK:NPSNY ) is the really cool way to play Tencent since the South African company owns a stake in the company. But two surface-level observations: all of these companies have done poorly in 2018, which is interesting given FANG is still more or less doing fine, the occasional bump aside. And I spoke recently with a China expert about BABA, to come out in a Behind the Idea podcast in early September, and we talked about how Tencent may be playing a central role in China's economy, but that it's still hard to actually understand what the company is doing and what the value is based on.
Where to go next - Reviewing these articles and the recent quarter report, and seeing what the underlying 'core' earnings and prospects are for Tencent.
Sentiment Check - Fairly one-sided, in the bullish direction.
Canopy Growth: Undervalued Canadian Cannabis King by Juan de la Hoz I confess there are some industries that I have not paid attention to. In fact, a few of the names we cover in this long ideas section are off my radar - defense, for example, or whatever Aerohive ( HIVE ) does. The pot sector is one I also just have not looked into, even as it has matured over the 6 years I have been at Seeking Alpha.
So I had no idea that Constellation Brands ( STZ ) had invested in Canopy Growth ( CGC ) and you probably could have fooled me as to who Canopy Growth is. Juan de la Hoz reviews the company in light of the $CAD5B investment, and valuation aside, it's a good outlook of the cannabis market and of Canopy's positioning.
There's also this statement - " Canopy's valuation is a tad rich. The company currently has a market cap of around USD $10B on negative income and cash flow and very few sales - $26 million in total last quarter." Yes, that is a rich valuation.
Where to go next - Who captures the surplus value in the cannabis value chain? Does the supplier get it, as with the tobacco industry? Are there barriers to entry for growing cannabis at scale?
Sentiment Check - We've only published one short idea this year, which was working ok until this news, as compared to six bullish authors.
Recent Underperformance Makes Northrop Grumman An Interesting Opportunity by Strubel Investment Management Strubel Investment Management often publishes skeptical pieces, so it caught my eye that they are bullish in this case. They point out that Northrop Grumman ( NOC ) has sold off ~20% and is trading at about a market multiple. Defense spending looks to be robust, and it seems reasonable that a market leader like Northrop would stick around. Strubel argues that one of the reasons for the sell-off may be that the company is focused on paying down debt and funding pension obligations rather than returning cash to shareholders. On the surface, that is a very promising sign - I would that all my stocks paid down debt and handled balance sheet obligations like that before returning cash. Strubel isn't pounding the table, but this becomes an interesting portfolio component.
Where to go next - As with the restaurants, defense stocks seem to be a well defined cohort, so it should be possible to compare and assess NOC accordingly.
Sentiment Check - Generally bullish, as I count five bullish authors in a row.
Aerohive: Fallen Angel About To Become Profitable by David Peltier I thought Aerohive ( HIVE ) might be defense oriented, or at least in aerospace when seeing this headline. Peltier's first article talks about the company, which is a wireless networking stock, and the opportunity that may emerge as it crosses into profitability.
The company actually is profitable on a free cash flow basis, though only because FCF adds back share-based compensation. One bit of hair is the company is not growing revenue currently, but Peltier cites management comments that we should see year over year growth in the second half of 2018. A FCF positive company with a good balance sheet - $1.2/share in net cash vs. $4.2 share price - is an interesting proposition, all told.
Where to go next - I have a hard time sussing out how important network equipment providers are in their respective vertical, so I'd want to learn that. Of course, the last time I did that was with Quantenna ( QTNA ), where I asked my dad about the company, and by the time I had an answer the stock had jumped on me. Alas.
Sentiment Check - The only author covering this is Vince Martin, and he gives a helpful and balanced take to add context to this one.
MagnaChip's OLED Bonanza Is Set To Continue by Shareholders Unite MagnaChip ( MX ) has popped up on value investor radars in the past. It had an accounting restatement in the past, and it has exposure to OLED sales. Shareholders Unite has covered the stock before, and in this quarter the boost in OLED sales appears prominently. The company hasn't yet translated this into consistent free cash flow, but Q2 was positive and promising in this regard.
Where to go next - How long is this tailwind for OLED sales? How assured is MX's position in this?
Sentiment Check - We don't get a ton of coverage on the stock, but the bias has been about 2:1 in favor of bulls over the past 2-3 years.
***
Thanks for reading this Idea Guide. The Idea Guide is published twice a week exclusively to Seeking Alpha PRO and PRO+ subscribers. If you have any requests, comments, or feedback, please leave them below, send me a direct message , or email me at daniel@seekingalpha.com .

Have a great weekend and finish to your summer.
Disclosure: I/we have no positions in any stocks mentioned, and no plans to initiate any positions within the next 72 hours.
